---
title: Critical app rollout gates
description: Stage production artifacts and verify ordinary API boundaries before moving production domains.
updatedAt: "2026-10-03"
audience: developers
---

Finance, Inventory, Contacts, CMS, and Tasks depend on the live Web API. A
successful satellite build does not prove that this shared dependency is usable.
Production releases must preserve daily enterprise operations during optional
download-provider failures.

## Ordinary operations and bulk downloads

Ordinary GET and HEAD requests never enter the optional offline-download guard,
even when `OFFLINE_DOWNLOAD_PROTECTION_ENABLED` is enabled. Explicit bulk
requests marked with the offline-download header retain their protection and
return a retryable failure when its provider is unavailable. Required MFA,
verified IP blocks, and baseline rate limits remain effective.

This rule applies to Web and the registered satellite API proxies. It prevents
optional Redis, quota, or Turnstile failures from blocking normal pages and
routine reads. It does not change permission checks or authorize bulk exports.
The real proxy regression suite is
`packages/utils/src/__tests__/daily-operation-download-isolation.test.ts`.

## Production domain assignment

The Web, Finance, Inventory, Contacts, CMS, and Tasks production workflows stage
production artifacts with `vercel deploy --prod --skip-domain`. They then run
`scripts/ci/verify-staged-critical-app.js` against the immutable deployment URL.
The gate requires production build metadata for the exact workflow SHA and app.
GET and HEAD probes with a deliberately invalid machine-key token must reach the normal JSON API authentication
boundary and return 401. Unexpected statuses, redirects, HTML, missing metadata,
and mismatched source identity stop the workflow before domain assignment.

Only a passing staged deployment is promoted, then recorded as successfully
deployed. [Vercel staging and promotion](https://vercel.com/docs/cli/deploying-from-cli)
retain the same built artifact. The CLI probe uses deployment-protection bypass
through [vercel curl](https://vercel.com/docs/cli/curl); it supplies no application
valid session and reads no customer records. Public `GET`/`HEAD` build metadata reads do not require satellite cookies.
CMS machine-key requests remove ambient cookies from the guard and forwarded
request, so invalid keys cannot borrow a browser actor and expired cookies do
not interfere with independent API-key verification. JWT-shaped headers retain
browser session refresh and assurance checks; their shape is not proof of
authentication. Public metadata reads discard incidental session credentials. CMS middleware
regressions cover metadata access, invalid machine-key forwarding, guard denial,
and browser assurance failures in `apps/cms/src/proxy.test.ts`.

When the production planner selects Web, every selected Vercel satellite waits
for Web's explicit `promoted` output. A failed, cancelled, skipped, or
package-release-blocked Web deployment prevents satellite rollout. When Web is
not selected, satellites can deploy independently. Cloudflare jobs keep their
own dependency rules.

These probes establish source identity and API ingress health. They do not prove
signed-in permissions, business CRUD, mobile behavior, or provider integrations.
The Web probe includes Learn's Programming catalog API: its sidebar page must
not advance against a platform artifact that lacks the route. An out-of-band
Instant Rollback can still create mixed versions, so recovery must restore a
compatible platform artifact and verify the signed-in Programming sidebar flow.
An HTML API 404 is not evidence that the Learn page or workspace is missing.
After promotion, verify the requested signed-in workflows separately and record
any missing evidence. Production database migrations still require their gated
exact-SHA workflow; never push them manually from an agent checkout.

Regression coverage lives in `scripts/ci/critical-rollout-workflow.test.js`,
`scripts/ci/verify-staged-critical-app.test.js`, and the existing release workflow
suite. The dependency test exercises selected and unselected Web, failed and
cancelled runs, missing promotion output, failed planning, and unselected apps.

## Lettin Worker health and cache initialization

Lettin uses the existing URL-pinned OpenNext adapter shared with Parley. Its cache
registration patch installs the composable handlers and returns before the
original Next `loadCustomCacheHandlers` loader. Replacing only minified declarations
leaves references to removed aliases; after bundling those names can capture
unrelated module locals and attempt to import `file:/.next/None`. This failure
occurs before `/api/v1/lettin/health` reaches D1 or R2 and can return an empty 500.

Run `node --test apps/lettin/scripts/opennext-health.node.mjs` after adapter or Next
updates. The regression patches and executes the installed Next production route
and page cache methods, registers the composable handlers, and rejects fallthrough
to the original loader. Lettin CI runs it before the real Worker build. Keep the
shared adapter patch and its exact URL dependency selected by the workflow matcher.

To distinguish the boundary from a storage failure, replay a retained artifact
privately with no outbound requests, local disposable D1 and R2, and a synthetic
`worlds(id)` table. Preserve the original and record runtime/version, normalization
and fixture changes. In the retained-artifact control, replacing only cache
registration changes health from empty 500 to 200; removing `worlds` then reaches
the health handler and returns its JSON `Request failed` 500. This proves the
cache boundary defect without establishing production storage health. Missing
retained WASM must be supplied from the matching installed Next package and
recorded as a harness dependency, not represented as original artifact bytes.

Require exact-commit CI, the emitted candidate Worker and hosted health verification
with deployment identity before claiming recovery. Keep production D1 migration
and authenticated workflow acceptance separate; an empty 500 alone does not
authorize database repairs.
